## Summary

Extends `benchmark/dsa` from a bf16, square-prefill, core-attention-only sweep into a config-driven suite that covers the lightning **indexer** as well as the sparse **core attention**, across:

- **phases**: `context` (prefill), `generation` (decode rows, batch × per-request kv_len × q_tokens incl. MTP), `bprop`
- **KV / index-key storage dtypes**: `bfloat16`, `mxfp8`, `nvfp4`
- **paged** variant (pool + block table; the kernels take flat ids, so paging is an id-mapping / locality change, not an API change)
- **models**: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (both indexer modes: `dense` and `hierarchical` = 16K-candidate consumer), GLM-5.3 / GLM-5.3-Flash, and a new opt-in Qwen3.8 QSA preset

Every (model, component, phase, dtype, paged) cell that no cuDNN FE kernel serves today is recorded as an explicit **skipped row with a reason**, decided by one pure function (`benchmark/dsa/support.py::decide_support`) in the runner before any subprocess is spawned. The nightly contract is preserved: the first 25 CSV columns, the 7-field `RESULT` line, the exit-3 skip convention and `<config>.webp` are unchanged, and `deepseek_v4` still expands to exactly the same 20 cases and labels.

## What runs today (verified on a cc 10.0 B200 and on a cc 10.7 board)

| component / phase | bf16 flat | bf16 paged | mxfp8 | nvfp4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| core context / generation / bprop | yes | yes | skip (no MXFP8 KV core kernel) | skip (no NVFP4 consumer) |
| indexer context / generation (dense) | yes | skip (dense keys only) | yes (Q and K e4m3 + UE8M0/32) | skip |
| indexer hierarchical (consumer) | yes (`SparseIndexerScoreRecompute` + `IndexerTopK`) | skip | skip (bf16-only) | skip |
| indexer bprop | yes | skip | skip | skip |
| Qwen3.8 QSA (all cells) | skip: no servable QSA kernel in this suite | | | |

Servable rows are identical on cc 10.0 and cc 10.7 (both map to the same kernel bodies): deepseek_v4 20/20 (legacy, unchanged), deepseek_v41 80/324, glm53 118/384, qwen38_qsa 0/168 (coverage rows, opt-in; not in `run_all.sh`'s default list). Full sweeps of the committed code: B200 612 rows → 120 success / 492 skipped / **0 failed**; cc 10.7 board all four configs, 896 rows → 218 / 678 / **0 failed**.

## Measurement notes

- Core TFLOPS are counted on the ids actually gathered (`sum(topk_length)`). Context and bprop rows keep full id lists over the whole KV range (the legacy meaning and the kernel's indexer-prefix contract); only generation rows use causal lists. Full lists cost the 32k core bprop ~18 % vs. causal lists at equal FLOPs (27.9 vs 23.6 ms on B200, reproduced on a re-run — the bwd scatter loses locality), so the table below supersedes the first-draft numbers.
- Generation rows run the prefill kernel as flat rows (one CTA per query row, no split-KV) and report `gather_gbps` on footer-inclusive bytes; this is labelled in `backend_detail`.
- Hierarchical rows time the consumer step (candidate-restricted scoring + top-k 512); the source layer's block top-k is not a cuDNN kernel and is not timed.
- mxfp8 indexer rows quantize Q and K (the kernel contract); bytes/token columns report the production storage formats (288/324/528/594/1024/1152 B records, 68/132/256 B index keys).
- `<config>_extended.webp` (one panel per component × phase) encodes a variant structurally — colour = KV dtype (second tone for a config's second model), lighter tint = paged, dotted hatch = hierarchical indexer, dashed edge = deterministic bwd — so styles never cycle, and its legend lists only variants with a served bar plus one hatched "skipped / failed" entry (second commit; the legacy `<config>.webp` is untouched).

## Measured so far (local runs; the nightly produces the official results/ artifacts)

| cell (bf16 unless noted; flat / paged agree within 1 % unless shown) | B200 (cc 10.0) | cc 10.7 board |
|---|---|---|
| dsv41_flash core context 2k, flat · paged | 0.358 ms / 480 TF · 0.358 / 479 | 0.130 ms / 1317 TF · 0.131 / 1316 |
| dsv41_flash core context 32k, flat · paged | 6.52 ms / 421 TF · 6.52 / 422 | 1.80 ms / 1527 TF · 1.80 / 1526 |
| dsv41_flash core bprop 2k → 32k | 1.25 ms / 344 TF → 27.9 ms / 246 TF | 0.457 ms / 940 TF → 6.46 ms / 1063 TF |
| dsv41_flash indexer context dense bf16 2k → 32k | 0.099 ms / 173 TF → 11.3 ms / 389 TF | 0.052 ms / 332 TF → 4.55 ms / 966 TF |
| dsv41_flash indexer context dense mxfp8 2k → 32k | 0.087 ms / 197 TF → 7.68 ms / 573 TF | 0.048 ms / 361 TF → 3.50 ms / 1255 TF |
| dsv41_flash indexer hierarchical consumer 2k → 32k | 2.18 ms (1.92 recompute + 0.26 top-k) → 34.9 ms (31.0 + 3.9) | 0.80 ms (0.68 + 0.12) → 12.2 ms (10.5 + 1.7) |
| dsv41_flash indexer bprop 2k → 32k | 0.239 ms / 108 TF → 3.89 ms / 106 TF | 0.092 ms / 280 TF → 1.21 ms / 341 TF |
| dsv41_flash core generation B=128, q=2, kv=8k and 128k | 0.066 ms, 3.1 TB/s gathered | 0.039 ms, 5.2 TB/s gathered |
| dsv41_flash core generation B=8, q=1, kv=8k and 128k | 0.029 ms | 0.021 ms |
| dsv41_flash indexer generation B=128, q=1, kv=128k: dense bf16 / dense mxfp8 / hierarchical | 1.26 ms (3.4 TB/s key scan) / 0.89 ms (2.5 TB/s) / 0.25 ms | 0.74 ms (5.8 TB/s) / 0.43 ms (5.1 TB/s) / 0.15 ms |
| glm53 core context 2k → 32k | 1.01 ms / 578 TF → 18.2 ms / 515 TF | 0.342 ms / 1709 TF → 4.89 ms / 1912 TF |
| glm53 core bprop 2k → 32k | (context phase only run locally) | 1.32 ms / 1118 TF → 19.9 ms / 1188 TF |
| glm53 indexer context 32k, dense bf16 / mxfp8 | 12.3 ms / 8.60 ms | 5.01 ms (877 TF) / 3.95 ms (1113 TF) |
| glm53_flash (pooled index, ratio 4) indexer context 32k, bf16 / mxfp8 | 3.02 ms / 2.14 ms | 1.21 ms / 0.85 ms |
| glm53 core generation B=128, q=2, kv=128k | (not run locally) | 0.095 ms, 6.7 TB/s gathered |
| deepseek_v4 legacy 20 labels (dsv4_flash, dsv4_pro; fwd + bwd) | (nightly artifacts unchanged) | all 20 served, e.g. dsv4_pro context 32k 4.08 ms / 2423 TF, bprop 32k 20.9 ms / 1182 TF |

Skipped rows carry their reason (`error_message`) and the storage bytes/token; no cell failed on either device. The cc 10.7 column is the full sweep of all four configs on the board (same commit, file hashes verified) at 2.42 GHz with the cooldown gaps; the B200 column is the local post-review pass of the committed code; the hierarchical consumer is honest but slow relative to dense (the recompute kernel scans the full 16K-slot width), flagged in the README as a kernel-side follow-up.

## Tests

- `python -m unittest discover -s benchmark/dsa/tests -v` — CPU-only contract tests (legacy pin, enumeration, skip matrix on cc 9.0/10.0/10.3/10.7, bytes/FLOP constants, id generators, RESULT parsing, CSV schema, charts).
- `cd test/python && pytest deepseek_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_DSA_benchmark_suite.py` — the same classes under `-m L0` plus a 6-cell GPU smoke (core context flat vs paged against the torch reference, core generation with two requests, paged core bprop, indexer mxfp8, hierarchical indexer generation, indexer bprop) with an allocation/sync honesty check.

## Follow-ups (documented in the README)

- QSA core attention through the cc 10.7 sparse GQA d256 kernel (natively paged, 4-token block lists).
- NVFP4 KV rows once a consumer kernel exists; MXFP4 / per-row-fp8 index keys.

+`--phase {context,generation,bprop}`, `--kv-dtype <format>`, `--paged` /
+`--flat`.

+indexer, compute capability 9.x or 10.x for the core backward, PyTorch with
+CUDA, `pip install nvidia-cudnn-frontend[cutedsl]` (or a development install
+of this repository's `python/` package), and `pandas`/`matplotlib`/`seaborn`
+for CSV and charts. `pynvml` is optional; with it each row records the
+dense-MMA peak at the sampled SM clock (`peak_mma_tflops`) and the legacy
+chart draws it as a dashed line. Pin one GPU with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`: the
+shared CuTe DSL compiler and the indexer APIs read the *current* device.

+### Axes
+
+A case is one point of
+
+```
+model x (s_q, s_kv) x backend x data_type x phase        (context, bprop)
+model x kv_len x batch x q_tokens x backend x data_type  (generation)
+    x component x kv_dtype x paged x indexer_mode x deterministic_bwd
 ```
-fwd FLOPs = 2 * s_q * H * topk * (d_qk + d_v)
-bwd FLOPs = 2 * s_q * H * topk * (3 * d_qk + 2 * d_v)

+| Axis | Values | Meaning |
+|---|---|---|
+| `component` | `core`, `indexer` | sparse core attention over the gathered rows, or the lightning indexer (scoring + top-k) |
+| `phase` | `context`, `generation`, `bprop` | prefill (one request, `s_q == s_kv`), decode / MTP rows over a long cache (batched), training backward. `profile_pass` stays `fwd` for context and generation, `bwd` for bprop |

+"""
+KV pools and top-k index lists for the DSA benchmark suite.
+
+The sparse core kernels gather flat ``int32`` row ids out of one ``(rows, D)``
+KV pool. This module builds the pool (flat or paged through a block table),
+the per-query id lists the kernels consume and the host-side causal counts
+the indexer FLOP model needs. Torch only; nothing here imports ``cudnn``.
+
+Id lists are generated in row chunks so no ``(rows x kv_len)`` tensor is ever
+live, with ``torch.argsort`` over each row's visible range only. The chunk
+shrinks automatically for long pools (a 128k-token request keeps the scratch
+at a few hundred MiB). The kernels' own buffers are a separate matter: the
+mxfp8 indexer disables microbatching and its candidate buffer grows as
+``S * (S + 1) / 2`` fp32 at ratio 1.
+
+Positions follow the FE indexer kernels' convention. A request's pool holds
+``kv_len`` tokens including the ``q_tokens`` being produced, so query row
+``j`` sits at position ``kv_len - q_tokens + j`` in generation and at ``j``
+in context (``q_seqlen == kv_seqlen``, offsets zero). :func:`make_topk_ids`
+draws causal lists (tokens ``<= pos``) by default; with ``causal=False``
+every row draws from the whole request (the core context / bprop rows: every
+query gathers the full top-k, the per-token upper bound). With index
+granularity ``g`` a row selects complete ``g``-token blocks and the block
+list is expanded to token ids; a causal row with fewer than one complete
+block gets ``topk_length = 0`` (the kernels clamp).
+
+The per-token byte footprints (:func:`record_bytes`, :func:`index_key_bytes`)
+are defined torch-free in :mod:`support` and re-exported here.

+# 32 Mi fp32 (128 MiB) plus the int64 argsort it produces.
+_CHUNK_ELEMS = 1 << 25

+class PagedPool(NamedTuple):
+    """A paged KV pool: ``pool (num_pages * page_size, D)``, ``block_table (num_requests, max_pages) int32``
+    and ``flat_index(req, tok)`` mapping a request-local token to its pool row."""
+
+    pool: torch.Tensor
+    block_table: torch.Tensor
+    flat_index: Callable[[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor]

+
+def make_paged_pool(
+    num_requests: int,
+    kv_len: int,
+    page_size: int,
+    head_dim: int,
+    dtype: torch.dtype,
+    device,
+    slot_order: str = "randperm",
+    spare_pages: int = 4,
+    generator: Optional[torch.Generator] = None,
+) -> PagedPool:
+    """Build a paged KV pool and the block table that addresses it.
+
+    Every request owns ``max_pages = ceil(kv_len / page_size)`` pages drawn
+    from ``num_requests * max_pages + spare_pages`` physical pages. With
+    ``slot_order="randperm"`` the pages are assigned in random order so the
+    gathers scatter across the pool as a serving allocator would place them;
+    ``"contiguous"`` assigns them in request order (pool row == flat row when
+    ``kv_len % page_size == 0``). Returns a :class:`PagedPool`; its
+    ``flat_index(req, tok)`` takes ints or (broadcastable) integer tensors and
+    returns ``block_table[req, tok // page_size] * page_size + tok %
+    page_size``. The pool values are ``0.1 * randn``.
+    """
+    if page_size <= 0 or kv_len <= 0 or num_requests <= 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"num_requests, kv_len and page_size must be positive, got {num_requests}, {kv_len}, {page_size}")
+    max_pages = -(-kv_len // page_size)
+    num_pages = num_requests * max_pages + int(spare_pages)
+    if slot_order == "randperm":
+        slots = torch.randperm(num_pages, device=device, generator=generator)[: num_requests * max_pages]
+    elif slot_order == "contiguous":
+        slots = torch.arange(num_requests * max_pages, device=device)
+    else:
+        raise ValueError(f"slot_order must be randperm or contiguous, got {slot_order!r}")
+    block_table = slots.view(num_requests, max_pages).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
+    pool = torch.randn(num_pages * page_size, head_dim, dtype=dtype, device=device, generator=generator).mul_(0.1)
+    table64 = block_table.to(torch.int64)
+
+    def flat_index(req, tok):
+        req = torch.as_tensor(req, device=device, dtype=torch.int64)
+        tok = torch.as_tensor(tok, device=device, dtype=torch.int64)
+        return table64[req, tok // page_size] * page_size + tok % page_size
+
+    return PagedPool(pool, block_table, flat_index)
+

+def row_positions(q_tokens: int, kv_len: int, phase: str) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Causal position of each of a request's ``q_tokens`` query rows (CPU int64).
+
+    ``context``: row ``j`` is token ``j`` of a ``q_seqlen == kv_seqlen``
+    prefill (the indexer kernels with zero offsets). ``generation``: the rows
+    are the last ``q_tokens`` positions of the ``kv_len``-token cache, so row
+    ``j`` sits at ``kv_len - q_tokens + j`` (the ``q_causal_offsets`` the
+    worker passes are ``kv_len - q_tokens``).
+    """
+    j = torch.arange(int(q_tokens), dtype=torch.int64)
+    if phase == "context":
+        return j
+    if phase == "generation":
+        return int(kv_len) - int(q_tokens) + j
+    raise ValueError(f"phase must be context or generation, got {phase!r}")
+
+
+def causal_visible_counts(q_tokens: int, kv_len: int, phase: str, ratio: int = 1) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Index keys each query row of one request may score (CPU int64, ``(q_tokens,)``).
+
+    Follows the FE indexer kernels' completed-group rule, ``k_local <
+    (offset + q_local + 1) // ratio``: ``n_vis(pos) = (pos + 1) // ratio``
+    (floor), clamped to the pool length ``kv_len // ratio`` (the worker's K
+    pool holds the complete groups only). The DSv4.1 reference model also
+    admits the open group (ceil), a difference of at most one key per row.
+    Used for the indexer FLOP count ``2 * H_idx * 128 * sum(n_vis)``.
+    """
+    ratio = int(ratio)
+    if ratio <= 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"ratio must be positive, got {ratio}")
+    pool_len = int(kv_len) // ratio
+    pos = row_positions(q_tokens, kv_len, phase)
+    return torch.clamp((pos + 1) // ratio, 0, pool_len)
+
+
+def make_topk_ids(
+    num_requests: int,
+    q_tokens: int,
+    kv_len: int,
+    topk: int,
+    *,
+    phase: str,
+    causal: bool = True,
+    index_granularity: int = 1,
+    block_table: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    page_size: Optional[int] = None,
+    device="cuda",
+    generator: Optional[torch.Generator] = None,
+    chunk_rows: int = 1024,
+) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Per-query gather lists into a ``num_requests x kv_len`` pool.
+
+    Returns ``(ids, topk_length)``: ``ids`` is ``int32 (num_requests *
+    q_tokens, topk)`` with row ``req * q_tokens + j`` holding unique ids inside
+    request ``req``'s own range, and ``topk_length`` is ``int32 (rows,)``. A
+    ``causal`` row at position ``pos`` (see :func:`row_positions`) may only
+    pick tokens ``<= pos``; when fewer than ``topk`` are visible the row holds
+    all of them first, is padded with ``-1`` and ``topk_length`` is the valid
+    prefix. With ``causal=False`` every row draws from all ``kv_len`` tokens
+    of its request, so ``topk_length == topk`` whenever ``kv_len >= topk``.
+    With ``index_granularity`` ``g`` the row picks ``topk // g`` complete
+    ``g``-token blocks ``<= pos`` and each block expands to ``g`` consecutive
+    token ids. Flat pools map token ``t`` of request ``r`` to ``r * kv_len +
+    t``; with ``block_table`` and ``page_size`` (from :func:`make_paged_pool`)
+    to ``block_table[r, t // P] * P + t % P``. Generated ``chunk_rows`` rows at
+    a time, the chunk shrunk so one chunk's scratch stays under
+    :data:`_CHUNK_ELEMS` elements.
+    """
+    g = int(index_granularity)
+    if g <= 0 or topk % g:
+        raise ValueError(f"topk ({topk}) must be a positive multiple of index_granularity ({g})")
+    if (block_table is None) != (page_size is None):
+        raise ValueError("block_table and page_size go together")
+    if phase == "context" and q_tokens > kv_len:
+        raise ValueError(f"context rows need q_tokens ({q_tokens}) <= kv_len ({kv_len})")
+    rows = int(num_requests) * int(q_tokens)
+    topk_sel = int(topk) // g
+    ids = torch.full((rows, topk), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    topk_length = torch.empty(rows, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    if rows == 0:
+        return ids, topk_length
+
+    # Visible complete blocks per row of one request, tiled over requests.
+    if causal:
+        n_vis_req = torch.clamp((row_positions(q_tokens, kv_len, phase) + 1) // g, 0, int(kv_len) // g)
+    else:
+        n_vis_req = torch.full((int(q_tokens),), int(kv_len) // g, dtype=torch.int64)
+    n_vis_all = n_vis_req.repeat(int(num_requests)).to(device)
+    req_all = torch.arange(rows, device=device, dtype=torch.int64) // int(q_tokens)
+    topk_length.copy_((torch.minimum(n_vis_all, torch.tensor(topk_sel, device=device)) * g).to(torch.int32))
+    expand = torch.arange(g, device=device, dtype=torch.int64)
+    if block_table is not None:
+        table64 = block_table.to(device=device, dtype=torch.int64)
+        page = int(page_size)
+
+    start = 0
+    while start < rows:
+        max_vis = int(n_vis_all[start : start + chunk_rows].max())
+        n = max(1, min(chunk_rows, rows - start, _CHUNK_ELEMS // max(1, max_vis)))
+        n_vis = n_vis_all[start : start + n]
+        width = int(n_vis.max())
+        if width:
+            scores = torch.rand(n, width, device=device, generator=generator)
+            col = torch.arange(width, device=device)
+            scores.masked_fill_(col.view(1, width) >= n_vis.view(n, 1), 2.0)  # invisible blocks sort last
+            take = min(width, topk_sel)
+            blocks = scores.argsort(dim=-1)[:, :take]
+            blocks.masked_fill_(col[:take].view(1, take) >= n_vis.view(n, 1), -1)
+            tok = torch.where(blocks.unsqueeze(-1) >= 0, blocks.unsqueeze(-1) * g + expand, -1).view(n, take * g)
+            valid = tok >= 0
+            req = req_all[start : start + n].view(n, 1)
+            if block_table is None:
+                flat = req * int(kv_len) + tok
+            else:
+                tok0 = torch.clamp(tok, min=0)
+                flat = table64[req, tok0 // page] * page + tok0 % page
+            ids[start : start + n, : take * g] = torch.where(valid, flat, -1).to(torch.int32)
+        start += n
+    return ids, topk_length

+"""
+Support rules and static per-case facts for the DSA benchmark suite.
+
+Every architecture / dtype / shape / API-existence skip rule of the suite
+lives in :func:`decide_support`, a pure function of the case fields and the
+compute capability. The runner evaluates it before spawning a worker (a
+skipped row costs no subprocess) and the worker re-evaluates it so a manual
+invocation gets the same answer; the worker keeps its exit-3 path only for
+declines the kernels raise themselves. The reasons are the suite's own
+wording, so no kernel message reaches a CSV.
+
+This module imports nothing beyond the standard library: the runner may run
+on a machine without torch or CUDA. The closed-form byte footprints
+(:func:`record_bytes`, :func:`index_key_bytes`) are defined here for the same
+reason and re-exported by :mod:`kv_pool`, which owns the torch generators.
+
+A *case* is a flat ``dict`` carrying the preset geometry (``num_q_heads``,
+``head_dim_qk``, ``head_dim_vo``, ``topk``, ``indexer_topk``,
+``num_kv_heads``, ``kv_layout``, ``index_granularity``, ``indexer_heads``,
+``indexer_pool_ratio``, ``mtp_rows``) and the case axes (``component``,
+``phase``, ``kv_dtype``, ``paged``, ``indexer_mode``, ``data_type``,
+``q_seqlen``, ``kv_seqlen``, ``batch_size``). The runner's expanded case
+(with a ``model`` preset and ``profile_pass``) is accepted too: missing
+geometry is read from the preset and missing axes take the legacy defaults.
+"""
+
+from typing import Any, Dict, FrozenSet, List, Optional, Tuple
+
+# (num_q_heads, head_dim_qk) -> indexer_topk values the sparse core forward kernels are built
+# for. Mirrors the forward API's variant table; the core rows of this suite are scoped to these
+# pairs so context and bprop rows pair up.
+CORE_VARIANTS: Dict[Tuple[int, int], Tuple[int, ...]] = {
+    (64, 512): (0, 512, 1024, 2048),
+    (64, 576): (0, 512, 1024, 2048),
+    (128, 512): (0, 512, 1024),
+}
+
+# Hierarchical indexer (DSv4.1 after layer 20): the consumer scores a fixed candidate list of
+# CANDIDATE_COUNT ids chosen by the source layer in CANDIDATE_BLOCK-token blocks.
+CANDIDATE_COUNT = 16384
+CANDIDATE_BLOCK = 8
+
+# Rows compiled through the shared CuTe DSL compiler (one target per device). The sparse core
+# forward compiles its own sm_100f image on every 10.x part and is exempt.
+SHARED_COMPILER_ROWS: FrozenSet[Tuple[str, str]] = frozenset(
+    {
+        ("core", "bprop"),
+        ("indexer", "context"),
+        ("indexer", "generation"),
+        ("indexer", "bprop"),
+    }
+)
+
+PHASES = ("context", "generation", "bprop")
+PROFILE_PASS_FOR_PHASE = {"context": "fwd", "generation": "fwd", "bprop": "bwd"}
+_PHASE_FOR_PROFILE_PASS = {"fwd": "context", "bwd": "bprop"}
+
+_GEOMETRY_DEFAULTS = dict(
+    head_dim_qk=512,
+    head_dim_vo=512,
+    topk=2048,
+    indexer_topk=0,
+    num_kv_heads=1,
+    kv_layout="shared",
+    index_granularity=1,
+    indexer_heads=0,
+    indexer_pool_ratio=1,
+    mtp_rows=1,
+)
+_AXIS_DEFAULTS = dict(component="core", kv_dtype="bfloat16", paged=False, indexer_mode=None, batch_size=1, data_type="bfloat16")
+
+
+def _get(obj: Any, key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
+    """Read ``key`` from a mapping or an attribute of a preset-like object."""
+    if isinstance(obj, dict):
+        return obj.get(key, default)
+    return getattr(obj, key, default)
+
+
+def indexer_topk_select(preset_like: Any) -> int:
+    """Index entries the indexer selects per query.
+
+    ``indexer_topk`` when the preset sets one (the prefix the core kernel
+    also emits an LSE over), otherwise ``topk // index_granularity``: 512 for
+    DSv4.1, 2048 for GLM-5.3, 512 four-token blocks for GLM-5.3-Flash and QSA.
+    Accepts a :class:`ModelPreset` or a flat case ``dict``.
+    """
+    indexer_topk = int(_get(preset_like, "indexer_topk", 0) or 0)
+    if indexer_topk:
+        return indexer_topk
+    return int(_get(preset_like, "topk")) // int(_get(preset_like, "index_granularity", 1) or 1)
+
+
+def case_fields(case: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """Flatten a runner case into the field dict :func:`decide_support` reads.
+
+    Geometry missing from ``case`` is read from ``case["model"]`` when the
+    runner's preset is attached, else from the legacy defaults; ``phase``
+    falls back to ``profile_pass`` (fwd -> context, bwd -> bprop) and the new
+    axes to their legacy defaults, so a legacy case needs no extra keys.
+    """
+    model = case.get("model")
+    fields: Dict[str, Any] = {}
+    for key, default in _GEOMETRY_DEFAULTS.items():
+        fields[key] = case[key] if key in case else _get(model, key, default)
+    fields["num_q_heads"] = case["num_q_heads"] if "num_q_heads" in case else _get(model, "num_q_heads")
+    for key, default in _AXIS_DEFAULTS.items():
+        fields[key] = case.get(key, default)
+    fields["phase"] = case.get("phase") or _PHASE_FOR_PROFILE_PASS.get(case.get("profile_pass", "fwd"), "context")
+    fields["q_seqlen"] = case.get("q_seqlen")
+    fields["kv_seqlen"] = case.get("kv_seqlen")
+    return fields
+
+
+def uses_shared_compiler(case: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
+    """True when the row's kernels compile through the shared DSL compiler (everything but the core forward)."""
+    f = case_fields(case)
+    return (f["component"], f["phase"]) in SHARED_COMPILER_ROWS
+
+
+def phases_for_config(cfg: Any) -> List[str]:
+    """Phases a config enumerates: ``cfg.phases`` or the list ``profile_pass`` implies.
+
+    ``both`` -> ``["context", "bprop"]`` (today's fwd then bwd), ``fwd`` ->
+    ``["context"]``, ``bwd`` -> ``["bprop"]``.
+    """
+    phases = _get(cfg, "phases")
+    if phases is not None:
+        return list(phases)
+    profile_pass = _get(cfg, "profile_pass", "both")
+    if profile_pass == "both":
+        return ["context", "bprop"]
+    if profile_pass in _PHASE_FOR_PROFILE_PASS:
+        return [_PHASE_FOR_PROFILE_PASS[profile_pass]]
+    raise ValueError(f"profile_pass must be fwd, bwd or both, got {profile_pass!r}")
+
+
+def record_bytes(head_dim: int, kv_dtype: str, kv_layout: str = "shared", num_kv_heads: int = 1) -> int:
+    """Per-token bytes of the core KV record in storage format ``kv_dtype``.
+
+    Shared record (K = V latent): ``bfloat16`` 2 * D; ``mxfp8`` D e4m3 + D/32
+    e8m0; ``nvfp4`` D/2 e2m1 + D/16 e4m3 block scales. Separate K and V:
+    ``num_kv_heads * 2`` such records. 512 -> 1024 / 528 / 288, 576 -> 1152 /
+    594 / 324, QSA (256, separate, 2 heads) -> 2048 / 1056 / 576.
+    """
+    d = int(head_dim)
+    if kv_dtype in ("bfloat16", "float16"):
+        one = 2 * d
+    elif kv_dtype == "mxfp8":
+        one = d + d // 32
+    elif kv_dtype == "nvfp4":
+        one = d // 2 + d // 16
+    else:
+        raise ValueError(f"kv_dtype must be bfloat16, mxfp8 or nvfp4, got {kv_dtype!r}")
+    if kv_layout == "shared":
+        return one
+    if kv_layout == "separate":
+        return int(num_kv_heads) * 2 * one
+    raise ValueError(f"kv_layout must be shared or separate, got {kv_layout!r}")
+
+
+def index_key_bytes(kv_dtype: str, head_dim: int = 128, pool_ratio: int = 1) -> float:
+    """Per-token amortized bytes of one index key (the indexer's K pool).
+
+    ``bfloat16`` 2 * D = 256; ``mxfp8`` D + D/32 = 132 (e4m3 + e8m0 per 32);
+    ``nvfp4`` D/2 + D/32 = 68, the MXFP4 (e2m1 + e8m0 per 32) production
+    format of the DSv4.1 indexer. One key covers ``pool_ratio`` tokens
+    (64 / 33 / 17 at ratio 4).
+    """
+    d = int(head_dim)
+    if kv_dtype in ("bfloat16", "float16"):
+        one = 2 * d
+    elif kv_dtype == "mxfp8":
+        one = d + d // 32
+    elif kv_dtype == "nvfp4":
+        one = d // 2 + d // 32
+    else:
+        raise ValueError(f"kv_dtype must be bfloat16, mxfp8 or nvfp4, got {kv_dtype!r}")
+    return one / int(pool_ratio)
+
+
+def bytes_per_token(case: Dict[str, Any]) -> int:
+    """Static per-token footprint of the row: the KV record for core rows, the amortized index key for indexer rows."""
+    f = case_fields(case)
+    if f["component"] == "indexer":
+        return int(round(index_key_bytes(f["kv_dtype"], 128, f["indexer_pool_ratio"])))
+    return record_bytes(f["head_dim_qk"], f["kv_dtype"], f["kv_layout"], f["num_kv_heads"])
+
+
+def static_columns(case: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """The appended :class:`BenchmarkResult` columns known before any kernel runs (every row, skipped ones included)."""
+    f = case_fields(case)
+    return dict(
+        component=f["component"],
+        phase=f["phase"],
+        kv_dtype=f["kv_dtype"],
+        paged=bool(f["paged"]),
+        batch_size=int(f["batch_size"]),
+        indexer_mode=f["indexer_mode"] if f["component"] == "indexer" else None,
+        bytes_per_token=bytes_per_token(f),
+    )
+
+
+def dsl_target_error(cc: Optional[Tuple[int, int]]) -> Optional[str]:
+    """Message when the installed CuTe DSL cannot target ``cc`` (or is below the package floor), else ``None``.
+
+    The one probe both the runner (once per run) and the worker consult; only
+    rule 15 reads it, on compute capability (10, 7) rows that compile through
+    the shared compiler. ``cudnn`` is imported lazily here so this module stays
+    importable without it; any import or probe failure reads as no verdict.
+    """
+    if cc is None:
+        return None
+    try:
+        from cudnn.frost.buffers import cutedsl_arch_requirement_error, cutedsl_state, cutedsl_too_old
+
+        message = cutedsl_arch_requirement_error(cc)
+        if message:
+            return str(message)
+        _installed, version = cutedsl_state()
+        return "CuTe DSL too old" if cutedsl_too_old(version) else None
+    except Exception:
+        return None
+
+
+def decide_support(case: Dict[str, Any], cc: Optional[Tuple[int, int]], dsl_target_error: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[str]:
+    """Reason this case is not served by the suite's kernels, or ``None`` when it should run.
+
+    First matching rule wins. ``cc`` is the device's compute capability as
+    ``(major, minor)``; ``None`` (no torch or no CUDA in the caller) is
+    treated as no capable GPU, so every architecture-gated row skips.
+    ``dsl_target_error`` is the runner's one-time probe of the installed CuTe
+    DSL (``cudnn.frost.buffers.cutedsl_arch_requirement_error(cc)``, or a
+    too-old marker); it only matters on compute capability (10, 7) for rows
+    that compile through the shared compiler. Reasons are the suite's own
+    wording and never quote a kernel message.
+    """
+    f = case_fields(case)
+    component, phase, kv_dtype, paged, mode = f["component"], f["phase"], f["kv_dtype"], bool(f["paged"]), f["indexer_mode"]
+    major = cc[0] if cc is not None else None
+
+    # Storage formats and precision.
+    if kv_dtype == "nvfp4":
+        return "no cuDNN FE kernel consumes NVFP4 KV or MXFP4 index keys (storage-format coverage row)"
+    if component == "core" and kv_dtype == "mxfp8":
+        return "sparse core attention kernels take bf16/fp16 KV; no MXFP8 KV core kernel"
+    if phase == "bprop" and kv_dtype != "bfloat16":
+        return "no low-precision backward kernel"
+
+    # Core geometry.
+    if component == "core" and f["kv_layout"] == "separate":
+        return "QSA-shaped GQA d256 separate-K/V sparse attention is not wired in this suite (cc 10.7 sparse GQA kernel is a follow-up)"
+    if component == "core":
+        pair = (int(f["num_q_heads"]), int(f["head_dim_qk"]))
+        if pair not in CORE_VARIANTS:
+            # The backward kernels accept more head counts, but core rows are scoped to the forward
+            # variant table so every context row has its bprop twin.
+            return f"sparse core kernels serve (num_q_heads, head_dim_qk) in {sorted(CORE_VARIANTS)}, not {pair} (core rows are scoped to the forward variants)"
+        if int(f["indexer_topk"]) not in CORE_VARIANTS[pair]:
+            return f"indexer_topk={f['indexer_topk']} is not a compiled prefix for (num_q_heads, head_dim_qk)={pair}; kernels take {CORE_VARIANTS[pair]}"
+
+    # Core architecture.
+    if component == "core" and phase in ("context", "generation") and major != 10:
+        return "sparse core forward requires compute capability 10.x"
+    if component == "core" and phase == "bprop" and major not in (9, 10):
+        return "sparse core backward requires compute capability 9.x or 10.x"
+
+    # Indexer rows.
+    if component == "indexer":
+        heads = int(f["indexer_heads"])
+        if heads == 0:
+            return "model has no indexer rows"
+        if heads not in (32, 64):
+            return f"indexer kernels require 32 or 64 query heads per KV head (model has {heads})"
+        if paged:
+            return "indexer kernels take dense BSHD/THD keys; no paged index-key input"
+        if phase in ("context", "generation") and major != 10:
+            return "indexer forward/top-k fused kernel requires compute capability 10.x"
+        if phase == "bprop" and major not in (9, 10):
+            return "indexer backward requires compute capability 9.x or 10.x"
+        if phase == "bprop" and major == 9 and heads < 64:
+            return f"indexer backward on compute capability 9.x requires at least 64 indexer heads (model has {heads})"
+        if mode == "hierarchical" and kv_dtype != "bfloat16":
+            return "candidate-restricted indexer scoring is bf16-only"
+        if mode == "hierarchical" and phase == "bprop":
+            return "hierarchical rows are forward-only"
+
+    # Per-request top-k against the pool (core rows: the gather lists hold ``topk`` unique ids of one
+    # request). Indexer rows never read ``topk``: they select ``indexer_topk_select`` entries and pad
+    # rows with fewer visible keys, exactly as every short causal context row is served.
+    topk, kv_seqlen = int(f["topk"]), int(f["kv_seqlen"])
+    if component == "core" and topk > kv_seqlen:
+        if phase == "generation":

+        return f"topk ({topk}) exceeds kv_seqlen ({kv_seqlen})"
+
+    # Shared-compiler target on compute capability (10, 7).
+    if cc == (10, 7) and dsl_target_error and (component, phase) in SHARED_COMPILER_ROWS:
+        return "installed CuTe DSL lacks the target for compute capability 10.7"
+    return None

+  them once more under L0 (enumeration pin, skip matrix, generators, parsing,
+  schema, charts). Nothing in them touches the GPU.

+  in-process (``benchmark_single_dsa.SETUPS``): core context on a flat and on
+  a paged pool against ``dsa_reference.ref_sparse_attention_forward`` (and
+  paged == flat bitwise through the same plan), core generation over two
+  requests, core bprop on a paged pool, the mxfp8 indexer context row against
+  ``check_ref_compressed_topk``, the hierarchical indexer consumer against
+  ``torch.topk`` over its own recomputed scores, and the indexer backward row

+  under ``torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")`` with the caching
+  allocator's allocation counter unchanged, so the numbers the suite reports
+  are the kernels' and nothing else's.

+    sys.path.append(str(_REPO_ROOT))  # nothing else provides `benchmark`; appending keeps the stdlib ahead of the repo root
+
+from benchmark.dsa import kv_pool, support  # noqa: E402
+from benchmark.dsa.tests.test_runner import (  # noqa: E402,F401  (collected here under L0)
+    ByteFootprintTest,
+    ChartTest,
+    ExtendedEnumerationTest,
+    FlopModelTest,
+    LegacyEnumerationTest,
+    PresetContractTest,
+    RunSingleTest,
+    SchemaTest,
+    SupportRulesTest,
+    TopkIdsTest,
+    WorkerArgvTest,
+)
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.L0

+
+def _gpu_smoke(fn):
+    """The GPU cells need the device to themselves; the imported CPU classes do not."""
+    return pytest.mark.gpu_exclusive(pytest.mark.xdist_group(name="gpu_exclusive")(fn))
+
+
+# The forward tolerances of test_DSA_sparse_attention_forward.py.
+_OUT_TOL = dict(atol=8e-4, rtol=3.01 / 128)
+_STAT_TOL = dict(atol=1e-6, rtol=2.01 / 65536)
+
+# dsv41_flash geometry at smoke size: 64 heads, d 512, logical K 512 with the full indexer prefix, sink, topk_length.
+_CORE = ["--num_q_heads", "64", "--head_dim_qk", "512", "--head_dim_vo", "512", "--topk", "512", "--indexer_topk", "512", "--has_sink", "--use_topk_length"]
+# dsv41_flash indexer geometry: 32 heads, one key per token, top-k 512 (the indexer prefix of K = 640).
+_INDEXER = [
+    "--num_q_heads",
+    "64",
+    "--topk",
+    "640",
+    "--indexer_topk",
+    "512",
+    "--indexer_heads",
+    "32",
+    "--indexer_pool_ratio",
+    "1",
+    "--has_sink",
+    "--use_topk_length",
+    "--component",
+    "indexer",
+]
+
+
+def _gpu_cell():
+    """The worker module and ``cudnn.DSA`` for a smoke cell, or a skip."""
+    dsa_utils._require_sm100()
+    try:
+        from cudnn import DSA
+    except ImportError:
+        pytest.skip("Environment not supported: cudnn[cutedsl] not installed")
+    from benchmark.dsa import benchmark_single_dsa as worker
+
+    return worker, DSA
+
+
+def _prepare(worker, DSA, argv):
+    """Parse ``argv`` as the worker would, apply the suite's support rules for this device, build and probe the cell."""
+    args = worker.parse_args(argv)
+    case = worker.case_from_args(args)
+    cc = tuple(torch.cuda.get_device_capability())
+    reason = support.decide_support(case, cc, support.dsl_target_error(cc) if cc == (10, 7) else None)
+    if reason:
+        pytest.skip(f"cell not served on this device: {reason}")
+    prepared = worker.SETUPS[(args.component, args.phase)](args, case, DSA, torch.device("cuda"))
+    prepared.probe()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return args, prepared
+
+
+def _assert_timed_closures_are_honest(prepared, repeats: int = 3):
+    """Run the timed steps as time_fn does (pre_iter outside, steps inside) under the sync-debug guard with no new allocation."""
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    before = torch.cuda.memory_stats()["allocation.all.allocated"]
+    previous = torch.cuda.get_sync_debug_mode()
+    for _ in range(repeats):
+        if prepared.pre_iter is not None:
+            prepared.pre_iter()
+        torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")  # any blocking D2H read inside a timed step now raises
+        try:
+            for step in prepared.steps:
+                step()
+        finally:
+            torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode(previous)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    allocated = torch.cuda.memory_stats()["allocation.all.allocated"] - before
+    assert allocated == 0, f"the timed closures made {allocated} torch allocation(s) over {repeats} calls; the timed region must be the kernels only"
+
+
+def _assert_full_unique_lists(ids, topk_length, pool_rows: int, topk: int):
+    """Every row holds ``topk`` distinct in-range ids (the full lists of the core context / bprop rows)."""
+    assert topk_length.tolist() == [topk] * ids.shape[0]
+    assert bool((ids >= 0).all()) and bool((ids < pool_rows).all())
+    ordered = ids.sort(dim=-1).values
+    assert bool((ordered[:, 1:] > ordered[:, :-1]).all()), "duplicate ids inside a row"
+
+
+def _check_core_forward_against_reference(v, indexer_topk: int):
+    q, kv, ids, sink, length, scale = (v[k] for k in ("q", "kv", "topk_idxs", "attn_sink", "topk_length", "softmax_scale"))
+    ref_out, ref_max, ref_lse, ref_lse_indexer = ref_sparse_attention_forward(
+        q, kv, sink, ids, topk_length=length, softmax_scale=scale, indexer_topk=indexer_topk, return_full=True
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(v["out"].float(), ref_out.float(), **_OUT_TOL)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(v["max_logits"], ref_max, **_STAT_TOL)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(v["lse"], ref_lse, **_STAT_TOL)
+    if indexer_topk:
+        # The worker keeps every row inside the indexer prefix contract (topk_length >= indexer_topk), so the
+        # indexer LSE is contractual on every row.
+        assert bool((length >= indexer_topk).all())
+        torch.testing.assert_close(v["lse_indexer"], ref_lse_indexer, **_STAT_TOL)
+    else:
+        assert v["lse_indexer"] is None
+
+
+def test_core_variants_table_matches_the_forward_kernel():
+    try:
+        from cudnn.deepseek_sparse_attention.sparse_attention_forward import api as forward_api
+    except ImportError:
+        pytest.skip("Environment not supported: cudnn[cutedsl] not installed")
+    assert support.CORE_VARIANTS == forward_api._SUPPORTED_VARIANTS

+@_gpu_smoke
+def test_gpu_smoke_core_context_flat_and_paged():
+    worker, DSA = _gpu_cell()
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    shape = ["--profile_pass", "fwd", "--q_seqlen", "1024", "--kv_seqlen", "1024"] + _CORE
+    args_flat, flat = _prepare(worker, DSA, shape)
+    assert flat.detail == "SparseAttentionForward.execute padded_K=512 indexer_topk=512"
+    v_flat = flat.tensors
+    assert v_flat["kv"].shape == (1024, 512)
+    # Context lists are full: every row gathers topk rows of the pool, so the FLOPs are the nominal rows * topk.
+    _assert_full_unique_lists(v_flat["topk_idxs"], v_flat["topk_length"], 1024, 512)
+    assert flat.flops == worker.flops_fwd(1024, 64, 512, 512, 512) == 2.0 * 64 * 1024 * 512 * 1024
+    _check_core_forward_against_reference(v_flat, indexer_topk=512)
+
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    args_paged, paged = _prepare(worker, DSA, shape + ["--paged", "--page_size", "64"])
+    assert paged.detail == flat.detail + ";page=64"
+    v_paged = paged.tensors
+    _assert_full_unique_lists(v_paged["topk_idxs"], v_paged["topk_length"], v_paged["kv"].shape[0], 512)
+    _check_core_forward_against_reference(v_paged, indexer_topk=512)
+
+    # paged == flat bitwise: the flat case's rows laid out through a block table, the same lists mapped through it.
+    table = kv_pool.make_paged_pool(1, 1024, 64, 512, v_flat["kv"].dtype, v_flat["kv"].device)
+    permuted = table.pool.clone()
+    permuted[table.flat_index(0, torch.arange(1024, device=permuted.device))] = v_flat["kv"]
+    mapped = table.flat_index(0, v_flat["topk_idxs"].long()).to(torch.int32)
+    run, probe, detail, v_mapped = worker._core_forward(
+        args_paged, DSA, v_flat["q"], permuted, mapped, v_flat["attn_sink"], v_flat["topk_length"], v_flat["softmax_scale"]
+    )
+    probe()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    for name in ("out", "max_logits", "lse", "lse_indexer"):
+        assert torch.equal(v_mapped[name], v_flat[name]), f"{name}: paged gather differs from the flat gather of the same rows"
+
+    _assert_timed_closures_are_honest(flat)
+    _assert_timed_closures_are_honest(paged)
+

+@_gpu_smoke
+def test_gpu_smoke_core_generation_two_requests():
+    worker, DSA = _gpu_cell()
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    _args, prepared = _prepare(
+        worker, DSA, ["--profile_pass", "fwd", "--phase", "generation", "--batch_size", "2", "--q_seqlen", "2", "--kv_seqlen", "1024"] + _CORE
+    )
+    rows = 2 * 2
+    bytes_gathered = rows * 512 * 1024 + rows * 512 * 4 + rows * 64 * (512 + 512) * 2
+    assert (
+        prepared.detail
+        == f"SparseAttentionForward.execute padded_K=512 indexer_topk=512;flat-row prefill kernel;rows={rows};CTAs={rows};no split-KV;bytes_gathered={bytes_gathered}"
+    )
+    assert prepared.flops == worker.flops_fwd(rows, 64, 512, 512, 512)
+    v = prepared.tensors
+    assert v["q"].shape == (rows, 64, 512)
+    assert v["kv"].shape == (2 * 1024, 512)
+    assert v["topk_length"].tolist() == [512] * rows
+    ids = v["topk_idxs"].long()
+    for row in range(rows):
+        req, j = divmod(row, 2)
+        own = ids[row]
+        assert bool(((own >= req * 1024) & (own <= req * 1024 + (1024 - 2 + j))).all()), f"row {row} gathers outside its own request's causal range"
+        assert own.unique().numel() == 512
+    _check_core_forward_against_reference(v, indexer_topk=512)
+    _assert_timed_closures_are_honest(prepared)
+

+@_gpu_smoke
+def test_gpu_smoke_core_bprop_paged():
+    worker, DSA = _gpu_cell()
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    _args, prepared = _prepare(worker, DSA, ["--profile_pass", "bwd", "--phase", "bprop", "--q_seqlen", "512", "--kv_seqlen", "512", "--paged"] + _CORE)
+    assert prepared.detail.startswith("SparseAttentionBackward.execute workspace_bytes=") and prepared.detail.endswith("deterministic=False;page=64")
+    assert prepared.flops == worker.flops_bwd(512, 64, 512, 512, 512)

+    for name in ("dq", "dkv", "d_sink"):
+        assert bool(torch.isfinite(v[name].float()).all()), f"{name} is not finite after the probe call"

+@_gpu_smoke
+def test_gpu_smoke_indexer_context_mxfp8():
+    worker, DSA = _gpu_cell()
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    # S = 1024 with top_k 512: rows 512.. select 512 of up to 1024 visible keys, so the top-k cut is exercised.
+    s = 1024
+    _args, prepared = _prepare(
+        worker, DSA, ["--profile_pass", "fwd", "--phase", "context", "--kv_dtype", "mxfp8", "--q_seqlen", str(s), "--kv_seqlen", str(s)] + _INDEXER
+    )
+    assert prepared.detail == "indexer_forward_top_k_wrapper precision=mxfp8 top_k=512 ratio=1 heads=32;fused"
+    assert prepared.flops == worker.flops_indexer_logits(32, s * (s + 1) // 2)
+    v = prepared.tensors
+    assert v["precision"] == "mxfp8" and v["microbatch_rows"] == 0
+    q, k, w = v["q"], v["k"], v["w"]
+    assert q.dtype == k.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn and w.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+    assert q.shape == (1, s, 32, 128) and k.shape == (1, s, 1, 128)
+    assert v["q_scale"] is not None and v["k_scale"] is not None and v["q_causal_offsets"] is None
+    # Unit E8M0 scales: the kernel scores the e4m3 values themselves, so the dense torch reference reads them directly.
+    dense = ref_indexer_forward(q, k, w, ratio=1)
+    indices, logits = v["out_indices"], v["out_logits"]
+    assert indices.shape == logits.shape == (1, s, 512)
+    check_ref_compressed_topk(dense, indices, logits, 512, atol=2e-3, rtol=2e-3)  # one request: global ids == local ids
+    # Causal: row j selects positions <= j only, all of them while fewer than top_k are visible, 512 afterwards.
+    pos = torch.arange(s, device=indices.device)
+    assert bool(((indices[0] <= pos.view(s, 1)) | (indices[0] < 0)).all())
+    assert torch.equal((indices[0] >= 0).sum(-1), torch.clamp(pos + 1, max=512))
+    _assert_timed_closures_are_honest(prepared)
+

+@_gpu_smoke
+def test_gpu_smoke_indexer_hierarchical_generation():
+    worker, DSA = _gpu_cell()
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    count, top_k = support.CANDIDATE_COUNT, 512
+    # Two requests whose caches hold exactly `count` tokens: every candidate slot is a valid position, so the
+    # recomputed scores are fully defined and the kernel's top-k can be checked against torch.topk.
+    _args, prepared = _prepare(
+        worker,
+        DSA,
+        ["--profile_pass", "fwd", "--phase", "generation", "--batch_size", "2", "--q_seqlen", "1", "--kv_seqlen", str(count), "--indexer_mode", "hierarchical"]
+        + _INDEXER,
+    )
+    assert len(prepared.steps) == 2
+    assert prepared.detail == f"SparseIndexerScoreRecompute+IndexerTopK candidates={count} block={support.CANDIDATE_BLOCK} top_k={top_k} heads=32;consumer"
+    assert prepared.flops == worker.flops_indexer_logits(32, 2 * count)
+    v = prepared.tensors
+    assert v["n_valid"].tolist() == [[count], [count]]
+    candidates = v["candidates"].long()
+    for req in range(2):
+        assert torch.equal(candidates[req, 0].sort().values, torch.arange(req * count, (req + 1) * count, device=candidates.device))
+    scores, selected = v["scores"], v["selected"].long()
+    assert scores.shape == (2, count) and selected.shape == (2, top_k)
+    assert bool(torch.isfinite(scores).all())
+    for row in range(2):
+        expected = torch.topk(scores[row], top_k).indices
+        assert torch.equal(selected[row].sort().values, expected.sort().values), f"row {row}: IndexerTopK differs from torch.topk over the recomputed scores"
+    _assert_timed_closures_are_honest(prepared)
+

+@_gpu_smoke
+def test_gpu_smoke_indexer_bprop():
+    worker, DSA = _gpu_cell()
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    _args, prepared = _prepare(worker, DSA, ["--profile_pass", "bwd", "--phase", "bprop", "--q_seqlen", "256", "--kv_seqlen", "256"] + _INDEXER)
+    v = prepared.tensors
+    op = v["op"]
+    assert op.topk == 512 and op.topk % 128 == 0 and op.block_I == 128 and op.topk_indices_global
+    assert prepared.detail.startswith("IndexerBackward.execute workspace_bytes=") and prepared.detail.endswith(
+        "backend=default top_k=512 heads=32;attn_score restore excluded"
+    )
+    assert prepared.flops == worker.flops_indexer_bwd(256, 32, 512)
+    assert prepared.pre_iter is not None
+    pristine = v["attn_pristine"]
+    assert not torch.equal(v["attn_score"], pristine)  # the probe call already overwrote the target in place
+    prepared.pre_iter()
+    assert torch.equal(v["attn_score"], pristine)
+    prepared.run()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    # grad_scale = loss_coeff / (B * S_q) * grad_loss = S_q / S_q * 1 = 1, the reference's unit scale.
+    check_ref_indexer_backward(
+        v["index_q"],
+        v["weights"],
+        v["index_k"],
+        pristine,
+        v["index_score"],
+        v["topk_indices"],
+        v["d_index_q"],
+        v["d_weights"],
+        v["d_index_k"],
+        sm_scale=1.0,
+        grad_scale=1.0,
+    )
+    _assert_timed_closures_are_honest(prepared)
